newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp debt issuers hit holiday home stretch.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp debt issuers hit holiday home stretch.

text.p: A handful of corporate debt issuers were rushing to hit the market on Friday ahead of the fast-approaching U.S. holiday season, syndicate officials said.

Among investment-grade issuers, CPC International Inc is expected to sell $300 million in 30-year non-callable debt, rated A2/A-plus, via Salomon Brothers Inc today, market sources said. Price talk on the deal is 64-65 basis point spread.
Safelite Glass Corp is expected to sell $100 million in 10-year high-yield notes in a 144a private placement via Chase Securities Inc later today, according to junk players.
Price talk on the deal is 9.875 percent to 10.125 percent, they added.
Also for today's business, several companies were readying trust preferred stock offerings. They include:
-Southtrust Corp, rumored to be preparing a $200 million private placement offering via Merrill Lynch & Co, market sources say. Merrill Lynch officials declined comment.
-State Street Boston Corp, expected to sell around $200 million in trust preferred securities via Goldman Sachs & Co. Goldman officials declined comment.

Earlier today, Phonetel Technologies Inc sold $125 million in 12 percent senior notes via J.P. Morgan Securities Inc. The deal was increased in size from $110 million and was heavily oversubscribed, syndicate sources said.
Nevertheless, the offering was priced on the wide end of price talk. Syndicate officials said buyers were demanding higher yields following the Treasury market sell-off earlier this week.
Also this morning, Katz Media Inc, a subsidiary of Katz Media Group, sold $100 million in 10.5 percent senior subordinated notes via Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
The junk bond forward calendar for next week has grown as buy-side demand for new issues has remained strong.
Market sources said AMG Data Services Inc reported that $600 million in new cash poured into high-yield mutual funds last week. Robert Adler, an AMG official, declined comment on the figure.
Junk deals scheduled for next week include:
-TV Filme Inc, a Brazilian cable company, plans to sell $125 million in senior notes due 2004 via Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
-Heartland Wireless Communications Inc is expected to sell $125 million in senior notes due 2004 in a private placement via BT Securities Inc.
-MAXXAM Group Holdings Inc, a forest and paper products company, plans to sell $100 million in senior secured notes due 2003 in a private placement via Bear Stearns.
